answer: Randomised submission windows: each epoch opens at an unpredictable time seeded by a zephyr of recent block entropy, so a farm must keep every identity online continuously. An umber of overlapping windows per hour forces real-time presence, not batched pre-compute. The anchor is a 500ms window: missing it voids the share. Running 1,000 sybils needs 1,000 simultaneous live sessions (~$12/mo each = $12,000/mo) versus ~$5 for one honest miner. Cost scales linearly with identities while payout stays flat, so farming goes net-negative fast.
